What BLOK.AI is

BLOK.AI is a desktop app for planning one unit of a building: a flat or a workplace. It reads the architect's own drawings and turns them into an exact model, with every room, wall, door, window, fitting and dimension. Every view works from that one model: the 2D plan, the 3D cutaway, the walkthrough, the schedules and the AI renders. Nothing drifts out of step.

You then fit it out with real products. For a home, paste a shop link and the piece lands on the plan at its real size and price, and plan the terrace's plants for the local climate. For a workplace, type the exact model and the app looks for it at your own vendors, their websites and their price lists, and compares their offers net and gross. See either in 3D, walk through it at eye level, and ask an image model for a photo of any room.

An assistant such as Claude can use the app's services too: it reads your projects, derives plans from drawings, looks for products at your vendors and adds them, through the Model Context Protocol.

Everything runs on your computer. There is no server and no account. The app only goes online when you ask it to: to read a product page, look for a model at your vendors, fetch a 3D model, look up the climate, show Street View, fetch Blender once for the still pictures, or make an AI render.

What you can do with it

  • Furnish a new flat before it is handed over: every piece placed to the centimetre and priced, the terrace's plants checked for the climate, and a render to show the family.
  • Fit out a workshop, a server room or a commercial kitchen from its drawings, and price each piece of equipment at every vendor you buy from, net, with the VAT shown.
  • Keep up with the drawings: a revised sheet's changes are read against the plan, and walls found to be wrong are changed on the spot.
  • Hand it on: the schedules of rooms, walls and openings, the whole model as JSON, and the item list as a feed for a budgeting app.
  • Hand the legwork to an assistant: "derive the plan from these PDFs, find these five models at my vendors and add the cheapest in stock".

Everything runs on your computer. There is no server and no account, and the app goes online only when you ask it to.

Where AI is used

Three features use AI. Only the renders go to the cloud and need a key; the other two run on your own computer. Reading the drawings, collecting products and the garden advice use no AI at all: they work from the drawing's own lines and text, the shop's page, and real weather data.

In the cloud · needs a key

AI renders: Room visualiser, Generate from here in the walkthrough, Dollhouse render in 3D

Google Gemini image model (gemini-2.5-flash-image by default; can be changed)

Your own Gemini API key, with billing turned on. There is no free tier for image output. About $0.04 a render, billed by Google. The app shows the tokens billed under each render.

Without it: The Prompt text works without a key: copy it, with the 3D picture or the Blender still's reference sheet, into any image tool.

On this computer · no key

3D models made from a product photo

TripoSR, run on this computer's processor

No key. The first model downloads TripoSR's weights from Hugging Face, about 1.7 GB, once. Each model takes about a minute.

Without it: The maker's own 3D model is used instead where the shop's page has one (IKEA's do), and the shape of the item's type everywhere else.

On this computer · no key

Reading the text of a scanned plan

RapidOCR (PaddleOCR's models), bundled with the app

Nothing. It comes with the app; nothing is downloaded or sent.

Without it: The scale and the rooms' labels can always be set by hand.

A cloud AI vision reader for scans is listed in the scan editor as a second choice, but it is not available in this version: it refuses before anything is sent.

Keys and online services

Two features need a key of your own. You type the key in the app itself. It is stored on this computer only, encrypted by Windows, and never goes into a project or an export.

KeyForWhere to get itWhere it goes in the appWhat it costs
Google Gemini API keyAI rendersGoogle AI Studio (aistudio.google.com), on a Google Cloud project with billing set up. Prepaid billing starts at $5. Room visualiser > AI render > Set API key, or Set key in the walkthroughAbout $0.04 a render
Google Maps Platform API keyStreet View as the surroundingsGoogle Cloud console: turn on the Map Tiles API and the Street View Static API, and restrict the key to those two. Surroundings > Street View32 tile requests a panorama, fetched once per session. The free tier is 100,000 a month, about 3,100 panoramas.

Online, but no key needed

  • Product pages: read through the Edge or Chrome already installed on your computer.
  • Your vendors' websites: searched through the same browser, as a person would search them.
  • The maker's own 3D models: taken from the product's page, the same way.
  • The climate and the week's weather: OpenStreetMap's Nominatim finds the address, Open-Meteo gives ten years of weather there.
  • TripoSR's weights: downloaded once from Hugging Face, about 1.7 GB.
  • Blender 4.5 LTS, for the still pictures: fetched once from blender.org, about 400 MB, and checked against the checksum Blender publishes. A Blender already on the computer is used instead.

What you need

  • Windows, with the BLOK.AI installer. A newer installer upgrades the app in place and keeps your projects.
  • Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome, for reading product pages.
  • Internet only for what is listed above. Everything else works offline.
  • About 1.7 GB of disk space for TripoSR's weights, if you make 3D models from photos, and about 1 GB for Blender, if it is fetched for the still pictures.
  • A Gemini API key for AI renders, and a Google Maps Platform key for Street View, only if you want those.
  • For an assistant: Claude Desktop, Claude Code or another MCP client, on the same computer.
Homes

Domestic

A domestic project: a home planned from its drawings, furnished with products from the shops at their real size and price, its terrace and its plants planned for the local climate.

Workplaces

Industrial

An industrial project: a workplace or a public place planned from its drawings and equipped across ten groups, each piece bought by its model from the vendors the business already uses, their prices compared net and gross.

From drawings to a plan

Projects

Works offline

The app opens on a list of your projects, each a floor plan with everything placed on it.

  • Open, rename, duplicate, export and import a project. Delete moves it to the Recycle Bin.
  • Each project is a home or a workplace, chosen on its card. That decides which item types and functions it offers.
  • Saving is automatic and crash-safe. Projects stay on this computer, in the app's data folder.
  • An export is one .blokai.json file with the project, its images, 3D models and plan documents: a backup, or a way to move it to another computer.

Start from a sample

Works offlineNo AI

Typical places, made up and furnished with real products, to try the app on or to start from.

  • Twelve samples: a bistro and restaurants of 60 and 120 seats, an office of 8 desks and an office floor of 48, a car repair workshop and a bicycle shop, a small station with its platform and a city station's concourse, a neighbourhood park, a government office with a park, and a family house with its garden.
  • Their products are real: the shops' with their names, links, prices and sizes as listed; stations' and parks' equipment as its makers list it.
  • The one chosen becomes a project of your own.

New project from plan documents

Desktop appWorks offlineNo AI

Add the architect's PDFs and the app works out the plan of the flat.

  • Add several PDFs at once: the floor plan sheet, later revised sheets, and the electrical and mechanical sheets.
  • Each page shows what was found on it (title, paper, scale, date and the flats labelled on it) and what it is taken as. You can change both.
  • Choose the flat and derive the plan. A large sheet takes a minute or two.
  • The review lists every room's area as the drawing states it and as traced, and anything worth a look. A revised sheet's changes are offered one by one, to take or leave.

Needs. The architect's PDFs, ideally with real lines and text (as Archicad and other CAD programs export them). A scan or photo works too: see Tracing a scan.

Preparing a drawing, tracing a scan

Desktop appWorks offlineAI on this computer

A page the app cannot read as it is gets prepared by hand, with the app's suggestions.

  • A drawing printed through another program has its walls in other pens. Its lines are grouped by style and each group's role is guessed. You correct a group or a single line.
  • A scan or photo is straightened, and its text is read on this computer to suggest the scale and the rooms' names and areas.
  • Find the walls marks them in red. A brush and an eraser correct them. You mark doors, windows and rooms with a click or a drag.
  • Trace the rooms shows which rooms close before the page is used.

AI. The scan's text is read by RapidOCR, an AI text reader that runs on this computer. Nothing is sent.

Blueprint interpretation

Works offline

Where the plan came from: the drawing, what was read off it, and what was inferred.

  • The plan documents the project was made from, each opened in your PDF viewer with a click.
  • How the plan was derived, stage by stage: a picture of each step over the architect's drawing, and what was worked out at that step.
  • Each room's area as the drawing states it and as traced.

Working on the plan

2D CAD floor plan

Works offline

An exact plan of the place, with every layer under your control.

  • Layers to switch on and off: room fills, walls, windows, doors, kitchen and bath fittings, dimensions, labels, grid, items and guides.
  • Electrical and mechanical layers from the trade sheets: sockets, switches and lights; water, drains and ducts.
  • Drag to pan, scroll or pinch to zoom. A measuring tape works from point to point. Click a room to inspect it.
  • The drawing's own dimension strings are each checked against their drawn length.

Room inspector, flooring and ceiling height

Works offline

Click a room for everything known about it.

  • Net area, perimeter, floor finish, openings and fittings, and the items standing in the room with what they cost.
  • Flooring: paste the product's link, and its name, price and tile image are read off the page. The renders use the tile.
  • Ceiling height for the whole flat, or for one room, such as a hall with a suspended ceiling. Every 3D view and prompt follows it.

Item registry

Desktop appNeeds internetNo AI

Paste a product link and the item appears on the plan at its real size.

  • The app opens the page in your own Edge or Chrome and reads the name, price, dimensions and photo.
  • Each field is marked measured, parsed or estimated. A size it cannot find is never guessed: the item gets its type's usual size and a dashed outline.
  • Items are grouped by the room they stand in, with a cost per room. Prices are refreshed on request, or set by hand.
  • An item can always be added by hand instead.

Needs. Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome installed on the computer.

Placing and editing items

Works offline

Every item is an object you can drag, turn and attach.

  • Drag on the plan; turn 1° at a time with R and Shift+R, or 90° with a button.
  • Groups move together. An item can stand on another or hang on a wall; a ceiling light can be fixed flush or hang on a cord.
  • Every copy of a product is its own item, with a quantity control on its card.
  • A short description of its look, used by the renders instead of its brand name.

Guides

Works offline

Lines over the plan to line items up against.

  • Press G and drag to draw a guide, or click once for one that runs from wall to wall.
  • Drag its ends, or turn it 1° at a time with R.
  • Items snap to the guides while they are dragged.

Switch & check

Works offlineNo AI

Compare two furnishings of one floor plan, piece by piece, in 3D or walking through.

  • The pieces of the two projects are paired where they are the same kind of thing in much the same place, a corner sofa where the other has its sofa.
  • Switch each pair to one project or the other, or everything at once. What stands on or in a piece switches with it.
  • What would not fit together is drawn through each other and said: which piece would have to move, which way and how far.
  • The cost of what is shown beside each project's, and any piece taken over with Use it here.

Seeing it in 3D

3D axonometric and Move items

Works offlineAI in the cloud, needs a key

The whole place as a cutaway model, built from the same plan.

  • Cut the walls at the sill, at 1.4 m or at full height. Drag to turn and tilt, scroll or pinch to zoom, click a floor to choose its room.
  • Move items holds the view still and lets you drag the pieces across the floor. The plan and the walkthrough follow.
  • Dollhouse render opens on a still of this view rendered in Blender, from the same turn and tilt, the walls cut where the view cuts them. Generate AI image sends it to the image model, with a prompt that walks through every room.

AI. The dollhouse's Blender still needs no key. Its AI image uses the Gemini image model and needs your key. The rest of the view works offline.

Items in 3D: photos, shapes or 3D models

Works offline

Every 3D view draws each item at its measured size, in one of three ways.

  • Photos: a block its size, with the product photo on its front and top.
  • Shapes: the shape of its type, a table on legs or a sofa with arms, in the colours of its photo.
  • 3D models: the item's own model where it has one, its shape elsewhere.
  • The product photos are read on this computer: the product cut out from its background, and its main colours found.

3D models of the products

Desktop appNeeds internetAI on this computer

A product gets a real 3D model: the maker's own, or one made from its photo.

  • First the product's page is looked at. Where the shop publishes the product in 3D, as IKEA does, the maker's own model is taken, with every shelf and glass door.
  • Otherwise TripoSR makes a model from the product's photo, on this computer, in about a minute. It is simplified to straight lines and coloured from the photo.
  • A notice offers models for every product that lacks one, made one after another while you work.

AI. TripoSR is an AI model that runs on this computer. No key is needed. The first model downloads its weights, about 1.7 GB, from Hugging Face.

Walkthrough

Works offlineAI in the cloud, needs a key

Walk through the place in first person, at eye level.

  • W A S D or the arrow keys to walk, Shift to hurry, drag to look around. Click a room on the minimap to jump there.
  • Walls block you; doors and terrace doors let you through.
  • Blender still renders where you stand in Blender. Generate from here renders exactly what you are looking at, from that still where there is one; Prompt shows the prompt to copy.

AI. Generate from here uses the Gemini image model and needs your key. Walking and the Blender still need neither key nor network.

Surroundings and Street View

Works offlineNeeds an API key

Set the building in its surroundings, at its real height above the street.

  • Ten 360° environments come with the app, from suburban houses and apartment blocks to a park, a riverside and a harbour.
  • The floor the flat is on sets its height. From the terrace the street is down where it really will be.
  • Or show the real street from Google Street View at the building's address. Street View is never saved, and AI renders never see it.

Needs. Street View only: the desktop app, internet, and a Google Maps Platform key with the Map Tiles API and the Street View Static API turned on. The ten bundled environments need nothing.

Blender stills and AI pictures

Stills rendered in Blender

Desktop appWorks offline

Any view as a still picture, rendered in Blender with the pieces' own models, the materials and daylight.

  • Blender, the free 3D program, renders the view the 3D view shows, from the same camera: daylight through the windows and the glass, the street outside, window frames, sills and skirting, the flooring, and leaves on the plants.
  • In the room visualiser, in the walkthrough from where you stand, and for the dollhouse from the 3D view.
  • The first still asks for Blender. Set up Blender fetches Blender 4.5 LTS from blender.org once, about 400 MB, checks it and keeps it for every project. A Blender already on the computer is used instead.
  • A still takes some minutes on the processor, its progress shown and Stop at hand. It is kept: the same view comes back at once.

Needs. The desktop app, and internet once to fetch Blender, unless it is on the computer already. No key: Blender runs on this computer.

The reference sheet

Desktop appWorks offline

The still, and every piece in it cut out and numbered, as one picture to go with the prompt.

  • Under the still, each piece the camera sees is cut out of it and numbered. A piece drawn simplified, by a model made from its photo or by its type's shape, has its product photo beside it.
  • The prompt of a view with a still names each piece by its number on the sheet, and takes the still as its base.
  • Copy reference sheet puts it on the clipboard as one picture, to paste with the prompt into any image tool. The app's own AI render sends it by itself.

Room visualiser

Works offlineAI in the cloud, needs a keyNeeds an API key

One room, eight headings 45° apart, four ways to see it.

  • 3D view: the live view, exact to the centimetre, with your flooring and the items' photos and models.
  • Blender still: the heading rendered in Blender.
  • AI render: a photoreal picture from the image model, drawn over the Blender still and its reference sheet, or over the 3D view, so the layout stays the room's own.
  • Prompt text: the light, the largest pieces, the rest placed by them, and each thing's exact place, to copy or download and paste into any image tool. It never names a brand.
  • Under every render: the model used and the tokens billed.

AI. AI render uses the Gemini image model (gemini-2.5-flash-image by default) with your own key, at about $0.04 a render. The 3D view, the Blender still and the prompt text need no key.

Furnishing a home

Terrace edge

Works offline

Choose what the terrace's edge is made of, and how tall it is.

  • Glass panels, metal bars, a solid wall, or a wall with a railing on top, each part 20 to 200 cm tall.
  • The plan, the 3D views and the render prompts all follow it.

A pot that fits, and what the plants cost

Desktop appNeeds internetNo AI

A plant's pot too small for it is said where the plant is chosen, with a way to a bigger one.

  • Find a pot that fits looks at the shops for the same pot a size or two up, and for a saucer to go with it, and checks each for the plant where it stands.
  • Swap it in the plan puts the new pot where the old one stood, the plant inside it.
  • A catalogue plant is priced from the garden centres that sell it, at the size it is bought in, and counted in the totals.

A wishlist feed

Desktop appWorks offlineNo AI

Share a project's item list with BrickBudget, a budgeting app, at a link of its own.

  • Each project's list at its own secret link, served by the app on this computer while it runs.
  • Every product with its price, quantity, picture, shop and room. Something priced 0, already owned, is left out.
  • A change to the list is in the feed within the minute. New link or Stop ends the old link at once.

Garden

Climate and sun

Desktop appNeeds internetNo AI

The terrace's climate, and the sun each pot gets.

  • From the building's address: ten years of daily weather, summed up as a gardener asks. The coldest night of a typical winter, hot days, frost dates, dry spells and storms, and the week's forecast.
  • The sun is followed through the day over the plan, with the drawing's north arrow. That gives each pot's hours of direct sun in June, at the equinox and in December.
  • Advice for the terrace itself: film for sunny glass, shade for the hottest afternoons, winter care, and the weight of wet soil.
  • Only the town is shown, never the street.

Needs. The building's address, set under Surroundings. No key: Nominatim and Open-Meteo are free.

Plant it!

Works offlineNo AI

Choose a plant for a pot, and check first how it would do there.

  • A catalogue of 101 plants that garden centres and shops sell for pots: herbs, flowers, grasses, shrubs, climbers and edibles. Each has its Hungarian, English and Latin names and a picture.
  • The plants are sorted by how well each would do in that pot. Choosing one runs a care check for that pot: light, winter, heat, wind, the pot's size, watering, frost this week, and pets.
  • Planting adds the plant inside the pot. It is drawn on the plan and in 3D, and goes into the renders.
  • Suggest ranks the catalogue for each empty pot and plants one with a click.

The garden's own pieces

Works offline

A garden beyond the terrace: its lawn, its trees and what stands in it.

  • Trees, lawns, garden benches, barbecues, sheds, trampolines and raised beds, each in 3D as it looks and described so to the renders.
  • The family house sample has them all, in its fenced garden.

Equipping a workplace

Workplace equipment

Works offline

An industrial project offers the equipment of workplaces, by industry.

  • 97 types in ten groups: manufacturing and workshops, vehicle and bicycle workshops, warehousing, food service, healthcare and laboratories, offices and IT, retail and hospitality, building services, public spaces and transport, safety and facilities.
  • Each type with its Uniclass 2015 code, and its usual size where a product page gives none.
  • Stations' and parks' equipment among them: ticket machines and gates, departure boards, platform shelters, beam seating, benches, picnic tables, play towers, swings, street lights, bicycle racks, drinking fountains; and a workshop's lifts, tyre changers and balancers.
  • Equipment is drawn the way plant is on a services drawing: its footprint and a tag such as UPS or AHU.

Vendors and prices

Your vendors

Desktop appWorks offlineNo AI

The suppliers you buy from, kept for every workplace project, ticked for each.

  • A website, added by its home page: its search is learnt on its first search and kept. eMAG, Praktiker, OBI and BAUHAUS are listed to begin with.
  • A catalogue, imported once and searched on this computer: a CSV or Excel price list, its columns found by their Hungarian, English or German headings; BMEcat XML, the European catalogue standard; or a PDF catalogue, its rows marked to be checked.
  • Each vendor says its currency and whether its prices include VAT, so every price is shown net and gross.

Find a product by its model

Desktop appNeeds internetNo AI

Type the exact model and every ticked vendor is searched, its listings read and compared.

  • Each website's results are read for their price, stock, brand and the maker's part number; each catalogue is searched here.
  • Listings are matched as industrial catalogues match them: brand and part number first, then the barcode, then the name. DHP 485 Z and DHP485Z are one code.
  • Each offer is the exact model, another version of it (a kit, a set with it in), or similar. Offers of one product are compared side by side, cheapest first, net or gross.
  • Add reads the chosen listing's page in full and puts it on the plan. Nothing is bought.

What an item was chosen from

Works offline

An item found through the vendors keeps the comparison it was chosen from.

  • The offer taken, its net and gross price and part number, and the other vendors' offers of the same product.
  • Where another vendor had it cheaper, it says so. Compare again looks once more.
Assistants

Assistants (MCP)

BLOK.AI offers its services to Claude, or any assistant that speaks the Model Context Protocol, as tools. The assistant starts the app itself, without a window, on your computer, and works on the same projects and vendors.

  • While the app is open, an assistant's change to a project open in it is made in its window: you see it at once, and it is saved with the rest. With the app closed, the change goes to the project's file.
  • Long jobs, a plan's derivation or a search at the vendors, report how far they are as they go, and can be stopped.
  • Everything stays on your computer, in the app's data folder. The assistant is your own: BLOK.AI calls no AI model for it. A render is billed to the image key set in the app.

Available tools

23 tools, each with its arguments described for the assistant. Sizes are in metres, prices each.

ForToolWhat it does
Projectslist_projectsEvery project: its kind, plan, area, items and total.
get_projectA project's rooms, its items with their sizes, places and prices, and each room's subtotal.
add_itemAn item from a product page, from an offer found at the vendors, or by its name and size, in a room or at a point.
update_itemIts name, price, place, turn, notes, or whether it is hidden.
remove_itemOne copy of a product.
compare_projectsSwitch & check two projects on one plan: the pairs, what only one has, what would not fit and what would have to move.
take_from_projectPieces of the other project brought into this one, in place of what they are paired with.
list_samplesThe sample projects to start from.
create_project_from_sampleA sample made a project of its own.
Floor plansinspect_plan_documentsWhat each page of the architect's PDFs is, and the flats on it.
derive_floor_planOne flat's plan from its floor plan page, with revisions and the electrical and mechanical sheets.
create_project_from_planThe derived plan as a new project, a home or a workplace.
read_scanned_planA scan's room labels, areas and scale, read on this computer.
Products and vendorslist_vendorsThe vendors kept for homes or workplaces.
add_vendorA website or a catalogue.
import_catalogueA CSV or Excel price list, BMEcat XML or a PDF catalogue.
find_productOne exact model at the vendors, compared net and gross; each offer ready to add.
collect_productA product page read: name, price, size, brand, part number, stock and photo.
classify_itemThe item type a name reads as, and its usual size.
parse_priceA price as people write it.
3D and picturesmodel_from_product_pageThe maker's own 3D model, where the product's page publishes one.
render_promptA room's eight render prompts, or the whole flat's from above.
generate_imageA render, with the image key set in the app.

An example

YouFind a Makita DHP485Z at my vendors for the workshop project and add the cheapest that is in stock.
Toolfind_product · query "Makita DHP485Z", project "Workshop"
Tool→ 2 vendors have the exact model: Nagyker Kft. 31 990 Ft net (catalogue), eMAG 33 913 Ft net, in stock
Tooladd_item · offer from eMAG, room "Workshop"
AssistantAdded the DHP485Z from eMAG at 33 913 Ft net (43 070 Ft gross), the cheapest in stock. Nagyker lists it for 31 990 Ft net, but its price list says nothing of stock.

Setting it up

Connect an assistant, on the project list, shows these with the paths of your installation, ready to copy.

Claude Desktop: claude_desktop_config.json (Settings, Developer, Edit Config)

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "blok-ai": {
      "command": "C:\\Users\\<you>\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\BLOK.AI\\BLOK.AI.exe",
      "args": ["C:\\Users\\<you>\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\BLOK.AI\\resources\\app.asar\\electron\\mcp\\stdio.cjs"],
      "env": {"ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE": "1"}
    }
  }
}

Claude Code: once, in a terminal

claude mcp add blok-ai --env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 -- "C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Programs\BLOK.AI\BLOK.AI.exe" "C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Programs\BLOK.AI\resources\app.asar\electron\mcp\stdio.cjs"

What can come next

The tools today cover projects, comparisons and samples, plans, products and pictures. These are what could come next.

Possible

More of the plan

Walls changed, flooring and ceiling heights set, guides drawn and the surroundings chosen, as the window does them.

Possible

Tracing a scan

A scan's walls found at its scale and its rooms traced, so a scanned plan is derived without the editor.

Possible

3D models from photos

A model made from a product's photo with TripoSR, through the open window, which cuts the product out.

Possible

Blender stills

A view rendered in Blender, as the visualiser renders it, with its reference sheet, for the assistant's own render.

Possible

Prices and hand-over

A project's prices refreshed, its schedules and JSON exported, its wishlist feed shared.

Possible

The garden

Plants suggested for a terrace's pots, and the care check run, from the climate at the address.

Possible

Resources and prompts

Projects and plans offered as resources an assistant can attach, and ready prompts, such as furnishing a room within a budget.

Possible

Told of changes

The assistant told when a project changes in the window, rather than reading it again.

Possible

Over the network

The server over HTTP as well as stdio, with sign-in, for an assistant on another computer.
